facts.text: Greater Sudbury is home to the world's largest integrated mining complex, with nine operating mines, two mills, two smelters, a nickel refinery and over 300 mining supply and service companies.
Health Sciences North is one of the largest employers in the region with 4,000 employees.
Glencore employs more than 1,200 permanent employees and supports another 1,200 contractors at its Sudbury operations.
Greater Sudbury is the most populous city in Northern Ontario and the largest city in Ontario by area.

overview: Greater Sudbury had 166,004 residents in the 2021 Census, up 2.8% from 161,531 in 2016. The median age is 43.2 and the median household income in 2020 was $84,000, higher than in most Northern Ontario communities thanks to well-paid mining and health care jobs.

Its 71,475 occupied dwellings are scattered across 3,186.26 square kilometres, the largest municipal area in Ontario, so customers are spread among many distinct communities. Operating mines and hundreds of mining supply companies give local businesses a steady industrial customer base.
